name: Light Jasper Red
lede: Light Jasper Red is a bright, coral-leaning pink named for jasper, close enough to our library's Rose Doree to be a near-duplicate.

sections.title: A light jasper, twice plated
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 atlas records this swatch twice: at plate XIII, hue 3′, tone b, and again at plate I, hue 3, tone b, both filed by the 1955 ISCC-NBS system in block 3, a deep pink [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates a close variant to about 1854, at plate 1, K 8 [1]. The library also records a third related name, Begonia, from 1892 [1].

Its nearest library neighbor is [[candy-pink]], and the closest core app color is [[terracotta]], about seven units away [1]. Ridgway's plates carry a near-duplicate he called Rose Doree, little over one unit away, close enough to call the same color under a different name [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pink in only 7 of 23,781 paintings, well under one tenth of one per cent [2]. The earliest match is a 1500 Baptism of Saint Zenobius by Sandro Botticelli, more than three centuries before Ridgway's plate, so that is a lookalike hue and not a pigment record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. With so few matches, no century or country pattern here is reliable [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and a match this rare is as much a coincidence of measurement as a real signal [2].
